name: clean
description: The dotnet clean command cleans the output of the previous build. It's implemented as an MSBuild target, so the project is evaluated when the command is run.

args.name: project
args.description: The MSBuild project or solution to clean. If a project or solution file is not specified, MSBuild searches the current working directory for a file that has a f…

name: -c
--configuration
options.description: Defines the build configuration. The default for most projects is Debug, but you can override the build configuration settings in your project.

name: -f
--framework
options.description: The framework that was specified at build time. The framework must be defined in the project file.

options.name: --interactive
options.description: Allows the command to stop and wait for user input or action. For example, to complete authentication. Available since .NET Core 3.0 SDK

options.name: --nologo
options.description: Doesn't display the startup banner or the copyright message. Available since .NET Core 3.0 SDK

name: -o
--output
options.description: The directory that contains the build artifacts to clean.

name: -r
--runtime
options.description: Cleans the output folder of the specified runtime. This is used when a self-contained deployment was created

name: -v
--verbosity
options.description: Sets the verbosity level of the command. Allowed values are q[uiet], m[inimal], n[ormal], d[etailed], and diag[nostic]. Not supported in every command.
